authority: uvp-core uvp-ir::canonical_stringify (serde_json number identity, ryu shortest round-trip formatting)
consumers: uvp-protocol packages/compiler canonical.ts must reproduce expectCanonical byte-for-byte
rules: Number identity is type-preserving: tokens without '.' or 'e' stay integers (u64/i64) and serialize bare; float tokens always serialize with a fraction or exponent.
An integral float keeps a trailing '.0' (100.0, never 100).

Floats render via ryu shortest round-trip: decimal form while the decimal exponent stays in [-5, 15] (1e-5 -> 0.00001, 1e15 -> 1000000000000000.0), otherwise scientific with lowercase 'e' and an explicit '+' for positive exponents (1e-7, 1e+16, 1e+300).
Object keys sort by code point; arrays keep order.

cases.name: integer token stays a bare integer
integral float keeps trailing point zero
exponent input spelling is erased to the canonical float form
large scientific float uses explicit plus exponent
decimal form at the lower edge
decimal form at the upper edge
scientific form past the upper edge
u64 beyond double precision stays an integer
keys sort by code point across number kinds
